findings.title: `_read`'s connection parameter is typed `Any` instead of `Conn`
findings.description: `_read` and the `read` closure in `tick_coverage` declare the connection as `Any` even though `manifest_reads.Conn` (`psycopg.AsyncConnection[Any]`) exists and is exactly what `connect_migrated` returns and what every callee (`build_status`, `build_coverage`) accepts. It works, but it removes the compiler's ability to catch a signature drift between the CLI plumbing and the build functions. A `Conn` alias import (under `TYPE_CHECKING`) would close it at zero runtime cost.

findings.title: `raw_counts` performs an unindexed scan of every `tick_trade` row in the range
findings.description: The `count(*)` join against `unnest` prunes to the touched hypertable chunks via `ts_event BETWEEN min(opens) AND max(closes)`, but within those chunks it scans every row (no index beyond the hypertable's chunk constraint) and evaluates the session-window join per row. This is the documented, deliberate "one scan" and is correct; for wide `--start/--end` ranges on a populated archive it will be the verb's cost driver. The module docstrings already promise slice-226 re-measurement — worth keeping that promise in mind for this query specifically.

findings.title: `_closed_port` in the status CLI test has a bind/close race
findings.description: The socket is closed before the port is used as an "unreachable" target, so another process could reclaim it between `_closed_port()` and the connect attempt; the test would then fail with a different error than the intended `TickDatabaseUnreachable`. Low probability on loopback and self-evident when it flakes, but a comment (or retry-tolerance) would help the next reader. The rest of the tier's DB safety (dedicated test URL fixtures, no production-variable reads) checks out.

findings.title: Coverage of a range outside the calendar's populated span exits 4, not 1
findings.description: `build_coverage` deliberately widens the calendar window by one day and lets `calendar_sessions`/`sessions_between` refuse (`OutOfPopulatedRangeError` → `TickCalendarError` → `EXIT_STORAGE`) rather than silently returning an empty report — consistent with the module docstring ("there is no degraded output"). However, an operator running `coverage --start 1999-01-01` gets exit 4 ("database unreachable") with a message about the populated span, which `READ_EPILOG` does not mention as an exit-4 cause. Behaviorally fine as designed; only the epilog text slightly under-describes it.
